title: The Narrows: Halifax, Two Ships and the Morning of 6 December 1917
subtitle: Halifax, Two Ships and the Morning of 6 December 1917
description: At 9:04:35 a.m. on December 6, 1917, the French munitions ship Mont-Blanc detonated in Halifax Harbour, leveling the Richmond district and killing nearly two thousand people. This narrative history reconstructs the catastrophe minute by minute, from the fatal collision with the Norwegian relief vessel Imo to the blizzard that buried the ruins. Drawing on harbour master logs, inquiry transcripts, and Relief Commission ledgers, the account traces the twenty minutes of fire that drew spectators to the waterfront, telegraph operator Vince Coleman’s final warning, and the relief trains from Boston. Beyond the blast wave, it examines the decades-long legal battle that divided blame between two captains and transformed maritime safety regulations. A chronicle of devastation and bureaucratic reckoning, this book grounds every detail in primary records to reveal how a wartime port disaster reshaped international rules for moving explosives and defined a city’s century of remembrance.

editorReview.text: This reconstruction of the Halifax Explosion is anchored by disciplined archival work, turning logbooks and manifests into a genuine narrative engine. The early chapters are particularly strong, building tension with precise physical detail and a masterful, time-stamped cross-cutting of perspectives on the harbor. However, the procedural rigor of its countdown structure wanes in the middle sections covering the inquiry and relief efforts, where the narrative retreats into summary and loses its concrete, multi-track immediacy.
